title: Trump family wealth gains
summary: Trump's 2025 OGE disclosure (released June 30, 2026) shows crypto as his largest income source. Reuters, the NYT and Bloomberg count more than $1.4B from crypto within at least $2.2B total; the AP counted about $1.2B, apparently before a Stablecoin Holdco (USD1) line of about $197M was added. The World Liberty share is contested at about $594M-$800M: Reuters/NYT report about $800M (more than $520M from token sales and more than $250M from selling interests), while Bloomberg, CNBC, NOTUS and The Block report about $515-529M from token sales plus only about $65-66M from the WLF Holdco equity sale. TRUMP coin licensing added about $635M. The Forbes figures are real but dated: Eric about $400M and 10x (Dec 2025), Don Jr. about $300M and 6x (Dec 2025), Barron about $150M (Oct 2025). Most TRUMP coin, WLFI and ABTC buyers are underwater. The filing shows revenue, not profit, so 'most profitable year' cannot be verified, and the loss data does not show investors were specifically American.

sub_claims.statement: Per his financial disclosure, Trump made about $1.4B from crypto out of about $2.2B, more than from any other business.
sub_claims.finding: The 927-page 2025 OGE filing was released 2026-06-30. The more-than-$1.4B crypto total holds: Reuters and the NYT report it, and Bloomberg corrected its own headline from $1.2B to $1.4B after adding a Stablecoin Holdco LLC line (about $196.9M from new capital contributions and the sale of units) that it had first left out. The World Liberty component is contested at about $594M-$800M. Reuters reports almost $800M from WLF: more than $520M from token sales and more than $250M from selling interests in the business. Bloomberg, CNBC (via IBTimes), NOTUS and others report about $594M: roughly $515-529M from token sales plus about $65-66M from selling equity in WLF Holdco. The Block itemizes $236.25M of token proceeds distributed by WLF plus $65.6M from the WLF Holdco equity sale. Our own arithmetic (no outlet states it): $65.6M (WLF Holdco) + $196.9M (Stablecoin Holdco) is about $262M, which matches Reuters' 'over $250M' from selling interests. So the gap appears to be whether the USD1 stablecoin entity is counted as World Liberty, not a disagreement about the crypto total. About $635M came from TRUMP meme-coin royalties via CIC Digital. Roughly $594M + $197M + $635M is about $1.43B. NYT: at least $2.2B total income, up from a minimum of $622M for 2024. Forbes: about $2.4B. AP: nearly $1.2B from crypto. Real estate, golf and resorts brought in about $500-575M, so crypto was the largest category. The form reports many entries as ranges, and all these figures are revenue/income, not profit.

sub_claims.statement: This may have been one of Trump's most profitable years ever.
sub_claims.finding: Forbes and the Daily Beast describe 2025 as his most lucrative year, at about three times the roughly $760M of 2024. The AP and NYT note the disclosure shows revenue, not profit, so profitability cannot be established. The claim's hedged wording ('may have been') is reasonable.

sub_claims.statement: Per Forbes, Eric Trump has gotten 10x richer since the election.
sub_claims.finding: Forbes (2025-12-04) estimated Eric at about $400M, 10x his level before the election. His American Bitcoin stake was worth about $160M at the time. Eric disputed the valuation without giving an alternative. The figure predates ABTC's further 87-95% slide, so it is probably lower now.

sub_claims.statement: Per Forbes, Don Jr. has gotten six times richer.
sub_claims.finding: Forbes (2025-12-08) estimated about $300M, six times his November 2024 level. He had been near $500M in September 2025, before ABTC fell.

sub_claims.statement: Per Forbes, Barron Trump is worth about $150M.
sub_claims.finding: Forbes gave this figure on 2025-09-22 (family tally) and 2025-10-06 (Barron profile). It assumes Barron holds about 10% of the roughly $1.5B that WLF added to the family fortune, with locked tokens heavily discounted. It is an estimate, not a disclosed number.

sub_claims.statement: The ventures that made the family billions have lost money for most of their actual American investors.
sub_claims.finding: TRUMP coin: Chainalysis counted 813K losing wallets (about $2B lost) in the first 19 days and about 764K losing wallets later. Nansen, cited by the NYT, counted about 989K wallets in loss (about $3.8B) by June 2026, with the token down about 97% from its peak. WLFI hit record lows of about $0.055-0.077 in April-May 2026, more than 80% below its peak. ABTC fell 75-95% from its Sept 2025 debut. So most retail buyers did lose money. Wallet data does not show nationality, however, so the 'American' framing is unsupported, and some revenue streams (licensing, USD1) did not involve retail losses.

corrections: Claimed: about $1.4B from crypto. The record shows: that is the Reuters/NYT/Bloomberg count, and it holds. The AP's figure of about $1.2B appears to leave out a roughly $197M Stablecoin Holdco (USD1) line; Bloomberg initially reported $1.2B and corrected to $1.4B when it added that line. All of these figures are revenue, not profit.
Claimed: $2.2B total. The record shows: that is the NYT's minimum figure; Forbes estimated about $2.4B.
The Forbes figures for the sons are from December 2025 and the Barron figure is from Sept/Oct 2025. They predate American Bitcoin's further collapse, so they likely overstate current values.
Claimed: most 'American' investors lost money. The record shows: the loss data covers wallets worldwide and does not show nationality.

The World Liberty share of the $1.4B is contested and is given here as about $594M-$800M, not a flat $800M. Reuters/NYT report about $800M, including more than $250M from selling interests. Bloomberg, CNBC, NOTUS and The Block report about $515-529M from token sales plus about $65-66M from the WLF Holdco equity sale, about $594M in total. The difference appears to come from whether the about $197M Stablecoin Holdco sale is counted as World Liberty. This is our inference from the figures; no outlet states it. The reading matches C42.
denials_and_context: White House spokesperson Anna Kelly: neither the president nor his family 'has ever engaged, or will ever engage, in conflicts of interest'. The White House says his assets are in a trust managed by his children, or in discretionary accounts run by independent institutions.
The Trump Organization called the filing 'one of the most comprehensive financial disclosure reports ever submitted'. World Liberty Financial declined to comment.
Critics note that Trump remains the beneficiary of the trust. Former acting OGE head Don Fox said every post-Watergate president managed his finances as though bound by conflict rules; Trump has not.
Eric Trump disputed Forbes' valuation of him but offered no alternative figure.
Direct fetches of Forbes, Bloomberg Law, The Block and the Daily Beast were blocked in this environment, so findings rely on search snippets that agree across multiple outlets.

changes: Sub-claim 1, summary, corrections, the WLF entity and the WLF->Trump relationship: replaced the flat about $800M World Liberty figure with a contested about $594M-$800M range, matching C42. Reuters (via The Star) confirms $800M = >$520M + >$250M. Bloomberg, CNBC (via IBTimes), The Block and others confirm about $515-529M + about $65-66M, or about $594M. The relationship amount_usd is now the lower bound, 594000000.

Added a likely reconciliation, labelled as our own inference: Bloomberg's correction note says it added a Stablecoin Holdco LLC line of about $196.9M, and $65.6M + $196.9M is about $262M, which matches Reuters' 'over $250M'. The two readings appear to differ only in whether the USD1 entity is counted as WLF.

Upheld the more-than-$1.4B crypto total. Bloomberg corrected $1.2B to $1.4B after adding Stablecoin Holdco, and $594M + $197M + $635M is about $1.43B. Recast the AP's about $1.2B as apparently missing that line; the AP article itself was not re-read.

The Forbes son and Barron figures were upheld. No newer Forbes estimates were found, so they remain dated. Direct fetches of Bloomberg Law, GV Wire and CAP were blocked, so this audit relies on search-result snippets.
